name: Consumer contract cooling-off and rescission periods by US state and transaction type
description: State-by-state comparison of the cancellation windows consumers have after signing specific types of contracts. Each record is one (state, transaction type) pair with the number of days the consumer has to cancel, the notice method required, refund timeline, and the statute citation. Covers transaction types that commonly carry cooling-off periods: home solicitation sales, health club memberships, timeshare purchases, extended warranties, hearing aid purchases, life insurance policies, dating/social referral services, credit repair services, membership travel, reverse mortgages, and door-to-door sales. The federal FTC cooling-off rule (16 CFR 429, 3 business days for door-to-door sales ≥$25) is the baseline; states add their own transaction types and periods on top. Answers 'how many days do I have to cancel a gym membership in [state]', 'what is the cooling-off period for timeshare purchases in [state]', and 'can I cancel this extended warranty'.
licence: US state government works — public domain. Federal FTC rule is US government work.

As a member of a health club, social referral club, or buying club you may cancel your membership in writing within three business days following the date on which the membership was attained.

records.transaction_type: debt management and debt settlement services
records.source_quote: Military Personnel Under a Minnesota law drafted by the Attorney General’s Office, military personnel may cancel cell phone or wireless service contracts without penalty when the service member is called to active duty. Military personnel may also cancel rental contracts, club contracts, service contracts, and membership travel contracts without penalty and receive a full refund of their deposit when a deployment or change in duty prevents the service member from using the service or abiding by the terms of the contract. Debt Management and Debt Settlement Services Contracts You may cancel contracts with debt management and debt settlement services providers at any time without cause by giving the provider ten days’ written notice.

records.source_quote: Minnesota law provides that motor vehicle service contracts—commonly referred to as extended car warranties—must allow you to return the contract within 20 days of the date the service contract was mailed to you, or within 10 days if the contract was delivered at the time of sale, or within a longer time period if provided by the contract. Upon return of the contract, the provider must grant you a refund of the full purchase price if no claim has been made under the contract.
